title: Predictive readiness windows using short-term load forecasts to stabilize autoscaler
creator: Miguel Ortega
description:
Problem: We observe frequent autoscaler thrashing during short traffic spikes and region failovers. Current readiness probes are reactive and binary which causes nodes to oscillate between Ready and NotReady during transient load. This leads to increased cold starts, elevated p99 latency, and SLO violations for multi-tenant customers during failover windows.

Proposal: Implement predictive readiness gating per-route that consumes a short-term (30s-5m) load forecast and a confidence interval to open/close readiness windows proactively. The readiness controller will: 1) subscribe to aggregated request-rate streams and short-term forecast metrics produced by a lightweight forecasting service, 2) compute a predicted capacity deficit relative to live capacity + warmup budget, 3) delay marking pods NotReady for transient negative deltas below a configured confidence threshold, and 4) when deficit exceeds threshold, trigger controlled shedding policies (per-tenant token-aware shedding and prioritized route degradation) while signaling autoscaler with a 'predicted_demand' metric to stabilize scale decisions.

Key behaviors: predictive smoothing (hold NotReady state for short predicted dips if recovery probability > 80%), confidence-based shedding (apply progressive shedding tiers at 90/95/99 percentile deficit levels), synergy with regional failover (regional forecasts cross-check to avoid global thrash), and safe-guards to ensure hard NotReady when sustained overload persists beyond the forecast window.

Why different: instead of tuning probe windows or adding static hysteresis, this ticket embeds short-term forecasting into readiness logic and ties it directly into the autoscaler's decision signals. The aim is to reduce oscillation while preserving SLOs and minimizing customer-visible degradation.
acceptance_criteria: Readiness controller consumes forecast stream and exposes predicted_demand metric to autoscaler
Observed reduction in autoscaler scaling events (target: >= 40% reduction in 1-3min thrash events in staging)
p99 latency regression <= 5% compared to baseline during synthetic failover tests
Controlled shedding activates only when predicted deficit confidence >= configured thresholds and follows tiered policy
Playbook updated and engineering-runbook created for disabling predictive gating in emergencies
metrics: predicted_demand (numeric): exposed to autoscaler and recorded in telemetry
shed_rate.per_tenant (%): when shedding enabled, measure affected token share
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag gated rollout: start disabled globally
2) Canary region: enable in us-west-2 for non-critical tenant set (5% traffic) for 48h
3) Promote to multi-region staging: enable across staging clusters and run synthetic failover / spike battery
4) Gradual production ramp: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% over 2-week window with QA gates after each step
5) Emergency kill switch: per-cluster FF to disable predictive gating and revert to baseline probe behavior
test_plan: Unit tests for forecast ingestion and confidence handling (edge cases: missing data, late data)
Integration test: end-to-end with forecasting service, readiness controller, and autoscaler in a single cluster
Chaos test: simulated region failover with cross-region forecasts to validate no global thrash
Load test: repeated 30s-3m spikes to validate thrash reduction and shedding behavior
Canary validation script: automated smoke checks and SLO comparisons to baseline
